title: HTML Injection via Error Query Param
summary: A sign-in screen reflects its `error` query parameter into the page as markup, letting an attacker inject arbitrary HTML through a crafted link.
author: Ovawatch Sec
brief:
**CloudDesk Portal** shows a friendly message on its sign-in page when a login fails. The message text is taken from the `error` query parameter and rendered into the page.

Because the value is treated as markup rather than text, an attacker can craft a sign-in link that injects arbitrary HTML — the foundation for phishing overlays and, depending on rendering, script execution.

> Local, intentionally-vulnerable app. Use it only on your own machine.
objectives: Trigger a failed sign-in and observe how the error message is shown.
Confirm the `error` query parameter is reflected into the DOM as HTML.
Inject benign HTML (e.g. a heading or styled banner) via a crafted link.
Explain how this enables phishing and where it can cross into XSS.

hints.text: Submit wrong credentials and look at the URL — the failure message travels in the ?error= parameter.

Replace the error value with HTML such as

hello

and reload — does it render as text or as an element?
If markup renders, an image with an onerror handler is the usual next step toward script execution.

solution:
## Root cause The sign-in view renders the `error` query parameter as HTML instead of text, so attacker-supplied markup in the link becomes part of the page. ## Proof of concept Inject markup with a crafted link: ```text /signin?error=

Account locked — call support

``` The injected heading renders inside the trusted sign-in page. Escalate toward script execution with an error-handler payload: ```text /signin?error= ``` ## Impact A single crafted URL lets an attacker paint convincing fake messaging onto the real login page (credential phishing) and, where the markup executes, run script in the application's origin. ## Fix direction - Render the message with `textContent` (or an escaped templating output), never as raw HTML. - Map error codes to a fixed set of server-side messages instead of echoing arbitrary input. - Add a Content-Security-Policy to blunt script execution if injection slips through.
